'''Masema Dagar''' (pronounced: mah-SEE-mah) was once a [[Shienar|Shienaran soldier]] who later became the Prophet of the [[Dragon Reborn|Dragon]].

== Appearance and personality ==
He was of average size. He had dark, deep-set eyes{{ref/book|c|Masema Dagar|comp}} and a triangular scar on one cheek.{{ref/book|3|1}}{{ref||comp}} As a Shienaran soldier, he wore his hair in a topknot.{{ref||comp}} As the Prophet, he kept his head shaved.{{ref||comp}}{{ref/book|5|39}}

He was generally unpleasant. He has no apparent sense of humor.{{ref/book|2|3}} As a soldier, he was prone to scowling and sneering. As the Prophet, he was mentally and emotionally unstable{{ref/book|5|39}}{{ref/book|12|p}} and quick to denounce anyone who did not live their life in devotion to the [[Dragon Reborn|Lord Dragon]] in the manner he thought right.{{ref/book|5|38}}{{ref/book|5|39}}

He considered [[Tinkers]] to be "useless cowards."{{ref/book|3|1}} He despised [[Aiel]].{{ref/book|2|10}}

== Activities ==
=== The Great Hunt ===
When he first met [[Rand al'Thor]], he regarded him with barely disguised contempt due to Rand reminding him of the [[Aiel]] he faced at [[Ankor Dail]].{{ref/book|2|10}} Shortly after the [[Amyrlin Seat]] arrived in Fal Dara, [[Ragan]] informed Rand that he couldn't leave the keep due to the order passed to him by [[Uno]], but implied that Masema's presence was the reason he wouldn't allow Rand through.{{ref/book|2|3}}

Masema was one of the Shienaran soldiers selected to accompany [[Ingtar]] in the pursuit of the [[Horn of Valere]].{{ref/book|2|9}} Masema and Ragan swam across the river [[Erinin]] to retrieve the ferry near where the flayed corpses of [[Changu]] and [[Nidao]] were found.{{ref/book|2|10}} When Ingtar's party encountered the Aielman [[Urien]], Masema immediately charged at him along with three other lancers until ordered to hold by Ingtar.{{ref/book|2|28}} When Rand, Ingtar, and the others visited [[Stedding]] [[Tsofu]], Masema was left just inside the ''stedding'' with most of the Shienarans.{{ref/book|2|35}}

After Rand transported the party to [[Toman Head]] via a [[Portal Stone]], Masema wept openly, presumably because of alternate lives lived.{{ref/book|2|37}} Masema witnessed Rand's fight with [[Ishamael]] at [[Falme]] and started treating Rand with religious fervor.{{ref/book|2|49}}{{ref/book|3|2}}{{ref/book|3|6}}

=== Becoming the Prophet ===
Following the [[Battle of Falme]], Masema and the other Shienarans accompanied Moiraine, Rand, and the rest of their party to the [[Mountains of Mist]].{{ref/book|3|1}}

After the [[Shadowspawn]] attack on their camp, Moiraine sent the Shienarans, including Masema, to [[Jehannah]] to meet with a contact of hers.{{ref/book|3|5}}{{ref/book|3|6}} After the [[Shienaran|Shienarans]] went to [[Ghealdan]] and found that [[Moiraine Damodred|Moiraine's]] contact was dead, Masema began preaching about the [[Dragon Reborn]], triggering civil unrest.{{ref/book|3|34}}{{ref/book|5|38}} He eventually attracted a crowd of nearly ten thousand people to hear him speak, who defeated the soldiers sent to disperse them.{{ref/book|4|47}} During this time, he provided the other Shienarans with enough to live on, even though [[Bartu]] and [[Nengar]] were the only ones who shared his particular fervor.{{ref/book|5|38}}{{ref/book|5|39}}

When [[Nynaeve al'Meara]] found him in [[Samara]], he had become the leader of a sect, asking his followers to abandon everything and follow the "Lord Dragon" (despite the irony that Masema had not seen Rand since early {{ne|999}}).{{ref/book|5|39}} He exercised control over large sections of Ghealdan, offering both refuge for the masses of displaced persons, and commanding a large body of [[Dragonsworn]]. He imposed harsh rules on not only his followers, but everyone he came across, requiring absolute devotion to the Dragon, and rejection of material possessions and worldly desires. He performed {{Wiki|Collective wedding|mass weddings}} involving hundreds of (often unintroduced) couples.{{ref/book|5|39}} While he strictly enforced the rules he set for his followers, looting, torture, and murder were common against anyone who was not vocal enough in their support for the Dragon, and for the Prophet. His followers were often described as dirty, wild-eyed, and feral.

By the time of Nynaeve's visit, Masema's influence was strong enough that the [[Alliandre Maritha Kigarin|Queen of Ghealdan]] would call on him, rather than him on her, and would discard jewelry at a mere suggestion by Masema.{{ref/book|5|39}} He had had Lord [[Aleshin Talvaen]], a member of the [[Crown High Council]], flogged for "contempt for the word of the Lord Dragon" and nearly beheaded Lady [[Baelome]] for a lack of respect when she referred to the Dragon Reborn as "this Rand al'Thor."{{ref/book|5|39}}

He seemed to live in accordance with his teachings, rejecting material wealth, living a modest lifestyle, wearing simple clothes, and eating simple food prepared by a widow from among his followers.{{ref/book|5|40}}

After Nynaeve's visit, both Masema and [[Galad Damodred]] independently sought a ship to carry her downriver.{{ref/book|5|39}}{{ref/book|5|40}} When the ''[[Riverserpent]]'' arrived, Galad's [[Whitecloaks]] seized the ship. This brought them into conflict with Masema's Dragonsworn. The resulting conflagration grew to envelop Jehannah and the nearby circuses, and resulted in an incursion into [[Amadicia]] on Masema's orders.{{ref/book|5|47}}

=== Rescuing Faile ===
When [[Perrin Aybara]] visited Masema in [[Abila]], Masema agreed to go with Perrin to meet with [[Rand al'Thor]].{{ref/book|8|30}}{{ref/book|9|1}} Upon learning that [[Faile]] had been captured by the [[Shaido]] Aiel, he and an army of his followers joined [[Perrin Aybara]]'s army in their pursuit. He even consented to [[Traveling]] to do so, despite his aversion to the [[One Power]] being wielded by anyone other than [[Rand al'Thor]].{{ref/book|9|6}}

While in Abila, he had secretly met with [[Seanchan]] representatives{{ref/book|8|30}} and was sufficiently aligned with them to receive a letter from [[High Lady]] [[Suroth]] instructing any who read it to aid Masema.{{ref/book|10|6}}

During the pursuit, Masema secretly met with [[Masuri Sokawa]] and [[Annoura Larisen]].{{ref/book|10|5}} The [[Aes Sedai]] hoped to use him,{{ref/book|14|44}} but Masema's motives remain unknown.

He reported to Perrin on a large quantity of grain found in [[So Habor]].{{ref/book|10|7}} He was with the Shaido prisoners when Perrin arrived and chopped off a prisoner's hand, looking for answers on [[Zarine ni Bashere t'Aybara|Faile Bashere]].{{ref/book|10|27}} Even he seemed shocked by Perrin's actions.{{ref/book|10|27}}

After Perrin formed a temporary alliance with the Seanchan, Masema aided Perrin in defeating the Shaido and rescuing Faile at [[Malden]].{{ref/book|11|29}} However, he also instructed [[Aram]] to kill Perrin.{{ref/book|11|30}} Afterward, most of Masema's army was dead or wounded due to a severe disadvantage against trained Aiel.{{ref/book|11|30}} He managed to survive and flee with about one hundred followers.{{ref/book|11|30}}{{ref/book|12|p}}

After he escaped Perrin's camp with his men, Masema planned to flee north and rebuild before returning to kill Perrin as ordered by one of the female [[Forsaken]] disguised as the "Dragon Reborn,"{{ref/tidb|537|3}} when "he" appeared "glowing in the air" the night before the battle. This strongly suggests Masema was at least partially manipulated by one of the [[Forsaken]] throughout his establishment of the Dragonsworn. He also began to question how he could have lost so many men. By this point he was fully insane, as evidenced by his internal monologue full of constant self-contradictions, such as believing his followers were both his precious, most loyal brothers, but also that they had failed him because they were cowards. He was killed by Faile and ''[[Cha Faile]]'' before he could follow through with his plans to escape.{{ref/book|12|p}}{{ref/book|c|Faile}}

===Aftermath===
In the wake of Masema's death, the [[Seanchan]] and the [[Crown High Council]] are re-establishing order in Amadicia and Ghealdan, respectively.{{ref|{{11|g}} - Prophet, the}}

==Parallels==
The name Masema bears resemblance to the Islamic false prophet "Musailma" and bears a resemblance to Musailma in the sense that they were both self-proclaimed prophets; just as Musailma was never a true Prophet of Islam, Masema too was a false prophet of Rand al'Thor.

Masema's hillside speech to a crowd of nearly ten thousand in Ghealdan bears some resemblance to Jesus' {{Wiki|sermon on the mount}} and other similar events.

The {{Wiki|Collective wedding|mass weddings}} performed with religious fervor is similar to the {{Wiki|Unification Church#Blessing ceremony|Blessing}} practice of the "{{Wiki|Unification Church|Moonies}}."

==In the television series==
In the [[The Wheel of Time (TV series)|television series]], {{TVlink|Masema Dagar}} was played by {{TVlink|Arnas Fedaravicius}}
